supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:57, WS-ICHEN-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01. The later PowerShell event uses the same logon ID, linking it to that session.
At 13:42:01, PowerShell ran the exact command to execute \\FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1, under sam.okafor's account. This matches the organization's stated workstation-patching practice.
The activity was followed by a Windows Update download through the proxy and a wusa.exe invocation for a Windows update package; PowerShell then terminated at 13:42:47.

The logged PowerShell activity is a strong match for scheduled business-hours workstation patching, and plausibly explains the reported brief PowerShell appearance around 13:40. The records establish process execution, not that a window was visibly displayed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show PowerShell process creation and termination, but do not establish whether its window was visible to ivy.chen.
The available records do not include the contents or hash of Apply-Updates.ps1, or a result confirming that the update installed successfully.
The reported time is approximate; the logged PowerShell start is 13:42:01 UTC.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not prove that the ticket reporter saw this specific PowerShell process.
The evidence does not establish the script's full behavior or whether the update installation completed.
unrelated_findings: For separate review: Firefox opened a Citrix StoreWeb URL at customer.cloud.com; the inventory does not list other remote-access services as approved. These records do not connect that activity to the alerted PowerShell execution. (T044-00163, T044-00171, T044-00172)
For separate review: Webex.exe was launched with an app.slack.com URL. This is not part of the alerted PowerShell activity. (T044-00168, T044-00170)

For separate review: services.exe and svchost.exe accessed LSASS on WS-ICHEN-01. The records alone do not establish whether those accesses were abnormal, and they do not connect them to the alerted PowerShell execution. (T044-00003, T044-00037, T044-00109)
